question:
A 77-year-old male patient seeks medical attention from his primary care physician due to a 6-month
history of fatigue and back pain. His medical history is unremarkable except for daily aspirin use. His
vital signs show: - Temperature: 98.0°F (36.6°C) - Blood pressure: 122/84 mmHg - Pulse: 90/min -
Respirations: 18/min Physical examination reveals lumbar spine tenderness, normal gait, and full
muscle strength in all extremities. Laboratory findings include: - Hemoglobin: 10.4 g/dL - Creatinine: 2.0
mg/dL - Ca2+: 11.2 mg/dL - Urine dipstick: 4+ protein, negative for blood A serum protein
electrophoresis demonstrates a prominent peak in the gamma region. What histological finding would
most likely be observed on this patient's kidney biopsy? Answer Choices: (A) Fibrin thrombi in
glomerular capillaries (B) Deposition of light chains within the glomeruli and tubules (C) Apple-green
birefringence on Congo Red stain (D) Glomerular crescents in Bowman’s space (E) Tram-track
appearance on silver stain (F) Podocyte effacement on electron microscopy (G) Thickened capillaries
creating a ‘wire loop’ appearance (H) Subepithelial humps on electron microscopy (I) Mesangial
proliferation with IgA deposition (J) Fibrosis and tubular atrophy with interstitial inflammation
 A. Thickened capillaries creating a ‘wire loop’ appearance
B. Subepithelial humps on electron microscopy
C. Fibrin thrombi in glomerular capillaries
D. Fibrosis and tubular atrophy with interstitial inflammation
E. Mesangial proliferation with IgA deposition
F. Glomerular crescents in Bowman’s space
G. Deposition of light chains within the glomeruli and tubules
H. Tram-track appearance on silver stain
I. Podocyte effacement on electron microscopy
J. Apple-green birefringence on Congo Red stain
